Exercise: Barbell Lunge

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_lower_body_pushing

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- hamstrings

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate to high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Knee instability or injury, reason: The movement may exacerbate knee issues due to the forward lunge motion.
- condition: Lower back pain, reason: Maintaining balance and proper form can be challenging, potentially straining the lower back.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Reverse Barbell Lunge, description: Perform the lunge in reverse, stepping back instead of forward.
- name: Alternating Barbell Lunge, description: Alternate legs with each repetition without returning to starting position.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Dumbbell Lunge, equipment: dumbbells
- exercise_name: Split Squat with Barbell, equipment: barbell

Instructions:

- This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
- Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
- Step away from the rack and step forward with your right leg and squat down through your hips, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: Do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. li>
- Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
- Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
